data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"If the divergence stratum is empty, no single-evaluation evidence can distinguish genuine gain from compliance: the problem is unsatisfiable by construction, and this negative result is itself the strongest available answer.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The divergence stratum is non-empty, making the negative result inapplicable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"An external or multi-evaluation source of evidence (e.g., longitudinal replication, mechanism inspection) is admitted, violating the single-evaluation constraint.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is non-trivial and the expert is imperfect but they nevertheless always agree, which would require an explanation beyond the trivial-or-perfect dichotomy.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"A corrupted-checklist control reveals a contrast even with an empty divergence stratum, because the corrupted checklist creates synthetic divergence.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Panel-level noise reduction itself constitutes a genuine reliability gain distinct from compliance, which would make the gain real even if not checklist-mediated.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The counterexample-first stance (SCR_001, SCR_005) establishes a hard boundary: when checklist and expert never disagree, the checklist is either trivial (codifying what the expert already does) or the expert is already perfect. In either case, panel outperformance cannot be attributed to checklist rule content within a single evaluation, because there is no case where the rule content could have made a difference. The set of possible single-evaluation observables is exhausted: performance, compliance, calibration, and confidence all collapse into either agreement or noise. The negative result is not a failure of method but a structural property of the problem space. This is an atypical candidate because it argues that the distinguishing-evidence question may be unanswerable in the very case the problem targets, rather than proposing a discriminating observable.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
